requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1 (bootloader/kernel command line includes audit=1)
requirements.summary: Baseline /proc/cmdline (cmd-59880c97093d4fd0) confirmed audit=1 absent. Executor applied audit=1 via grubby --update-kernel=ALL (cmd-024426780c654b46), verified in grubby --info=ALL output and the BLS entry file /boot/loader/entries/*.conf. Post-reboot /proc/cmdline (cmd-e61d1b232b684db3) directly shows 'audit=1' present on the live kernel command line, confirming the parameter is actually active at boot, not just configured.

requirements.requirement: Setting persists across reboots (survives an actual restart, not just static config)
requirements.summary: A genuine reboot was demonstrated: boot_id changed from cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 (pre-restart, cmd-8531616836cc4ad6) to cd5e4eb8-4f29-4bb7-8197-f756bb31e5c7 (post-restart, cmd-e61d1b232b684db3), corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots, which independently confirm the same transition. The restart was acknowledged via sudo shutdown -r now (cmd-ed9624a3c1524291), connectivity was lost (cmd-077fa2829c494d8c) then restored (cmd-aa9161cdd3b1482c), and post-restart cmdline shows audit=1 persisted through the real reboot, satisfying the required healthy-baseline to disruption to restoration to recovered-state transition for this persistence claim.

requirements.requirement: GRUB default config (/etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX) also updated to keep the change consistent for future kernel installs
requirements.summary: Executor updated GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub to append audit=1 (cmd-024426780c654b46), noticed an accidental duplication ('audit=1 audit=1'), and corrected it in a follow-up command (cmd-357dab7ccdf84ea9), leaving a clean single audit=1 entry confirmed by grep output.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured audit=1 via grubby (BLS entry) and /etc/default/grub, and proved persistence with a real reboot: pre-restart boot_id and cmdline (no audit=1) were captured, a genuine restart occurred (boot_id changed), and the post-restart live /proc/cmdline shows audit=1 present, directly satisfying the task's persistence requirement rather than relying on config alone. This restart also serves as adequate node-restart evidence for the sole managed node, cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. A minor self-corrected duplicate-flag bug in /etc/default/grub was fixed within the same attempt and left no residue.
limitations: auditd service itself is inactive post-reboot (systemctl is-active auditd -> inactive), but the task only required the audit=1 kernel boot parameter, not a running auditd service, so this is not treated as a gap.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured; multiple reboot cycles were not tested, though one full pre/post transition is sufficient to demonstrate persistence as required.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is short (8 commands) and each state-changing action maps directly to the task: baseline capture (read-only), grubby update, /etc/default/grub edit with a self-corrected duplicate-flag bug (cmd-024426780c654b46 -> cmd-357dab7ccdf84ea9, fully resolved within the same attempt, no lingering duplication), the required reboot (cmd-ed9624a3c1524291), and final verification (read-only). No unrelated services were touched, no failed units appear before or after (global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services and global:after_executor:node1:failed-services both empty), listening sockets are unchanged apart from expected PID churn from the reboot, and package health remained consistent (dnf, no changes). A backup file /etc/default/grub.bak was created by cmd-024426780c654b46 as a safety copy before editing; it is minor, expected practice, and not flagged as residue of concern. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found.
